_comment: Adversarial-review dispositions for the SIM-RESID domain, read by tools/migration_loop.py's review_gate(). A function the manifest flags review_required (writes a roster region OR size>p90 OR is root) may not be promoted to `verified` without an entry here. Shape: "<function name>": {"disposition": "reviewed"|"exempt", "session": "<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>", "by": "<reimpl-verify workflow / agent>", "note": "<evidence, or why no shadow/review applies>"}. A `reviewed` entry MUST name the `session` that ran the review: the driver cross-checks that that session's captured agents (session_reports/loop/<session>/agents.json) actually include an adversarial-review spawn -- a bare `reviewed` with no spawn is rejected. An `exempt` entry needs no agent (it is an explicit human-auditable decision). Keys beginning with _ are comments. Two layers read this file: migration_loop.py gates the TRANSITION to verified per session and cross-checks agent backing; migration_session.py --end fails while ANY review_required+verified row lacks a disposition, so a skip is caught in-session.
_created: 2026-08-31, empty, alongside tools/data/sim_resid_loop_prompt.md. Created rather than left absent so the first loop session finds the shape instead of inventing it -- 17 of the 39 ledger rows carry review_required, so this gate WILL fire on the first batch. There are no grandfather entries: unlike sim, no sim_resid row was verified before the gate existed, so every disposition here has to be earned.
_do_not_exempt_for_this_reason: T3 (armed differential) is unavailable for almost every row in this domain -- 37 of 39 members run once per run at session entry, and their write closures reach effectful callees. That is the DOMAIN'S NORMAL CONDITION, not a reason to exempt: exempting on it would empty the gate in one pass. With T3 off the table, adversarial review is HALF the evidence behind every `verified` here, which makes this ledger more load-bearing than sim's, not less. `exempt` is for a body genuinely covered exhaustively by the offline oracle, and the note must say which paths.

llm_strat_session_begin_multi.by: .claude/workflows/reimpl-verify.js (mode grouped, 3 lens-group reviewers + adjudicator per function, model sonnet; 14 agents, 1.28M tokens)
llm_strat_session_begin_multi.note: Verdict `diverges` -> TWO CONFIRMED divergences, both fixed and both re-verified against the .asm by the conductor before acting. (1) `MOV dword ptr [0x00be1a40],0x1f` @0x004543cd targets System's int-index 4 (base 0x00be1a30 + 0x10), not index 1. The translation AND its oracle both encoded 1, because both read the slot number off the Ghidra draft's field NAME (`planets[1]`) rather than off the address -- and sim_land_players_on_planet.cpp already warns that name is untrustworthy since cfg_final_struct_System is anchored 8 bytes late. Index 1 is 0x00be1a34, the define_index/name field three other functions read as a G_TEXT_PTRS index, so the bug both failed to set the intended cell and clobbered a live one. AN ORACLE THAT SHARES THE TRANSLATION'S PREMISE CANNOT FAIL ON IT: no mutation of that file would ever have caught this, which is the whole argument for adversarial review in a T2-ceiling domain. Oracle corrected to index 4 and given a negative arm asserting index 1 is UNTOUCHED; mutating the constant back to 1 now turns both red. (2) `const int32_t me = *v.player_side` sign-extends where 0x00454398's MOVZX zero-extends -- and the other two PlayerSide reads in the SAME function already cast through unsigned, so this was an internal inconsistency. Unreachable (the lobby bounds the slot to 0..7) but fixed per Law 2. Both introduced by the conductor's own 1740 edit replacing the writer's proposed system_planet_slot_mut(0,1) accessor with the generic one.
